sources.entry: Phoenix - Lightweight macOS window and app manager scriptable with JavaScript.

summary.one_liner: Phoenix is a lightweight macOS window and app manager that is scripted in JavaScript (or TypeScript compiled to JavaScript).
summary.what_it_does: Phoenix runs on the macOS status bar or as a background daemon and reads a user script, typically at ~/.phoenix.js. The script can bind keyboard shortcuts and system events to callback functions. Through these callbacks it can control screens, spaces, mouse, apps and windows. It can also log messages, show notifications, display content or ask for input with modals, and run external commands. The README says it aims for efficiency and a very small footprint. Configurations from versions 1.5 and earlier are not compatible with 2.0.
use_cases: scripting window placement and resizing on macOS
binding global keyboard shortcuts to window actions
writing a custom window management setup in TypeScript
running shell commands from keyboard shortcuts on macOS
how_to_run: Download Phoenix from the releases page and drag it to the Applications folder
Launch Phoenix and enable it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility
Write your script in ~/.phoenix.js (created on first launch)
For development: open Phoenix.xcworkspace in Xcode 16 or higher
Command-line build: xcodebuild -workspace Phoenix.xcworkspace -scheme Phoenix -configuration Release SYMROOT="$PWD/build/" clean build
notable: Scripted entirely in JavaScript, with TypeScript supported through compilation
Binds keyboard shortcuts and system events to user callbacks
Covers screens, spaces, mouse, apps and windows
Small footprint, runs from the status bar or as a background daemon
Bundled minified JavaScript library (phoenix-min.js) built from library/src
caveats: Needs Accessibility permission and an admin account to enable it
Configurations from versions 1.5 and earlier do not work with 2.0 and must be changed
